approval_timeline.simple: Commercial TI/addition/remodel scopes usually require plan review; expect at least several business days to a few weeks depending on completeness, valuation, and local queue.

checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in ID
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications

Confirm the required license is active and the contractor's license number must appear on the application. Gas piping/appliance connection work must be covered by the properly licensed contractor for that trade. Owner-builders should not assume they can pull this commercial permit.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of Boise Building Division

common_mistakes: Forgetting the gas reconnection scope and trying to close the permit without a gas inspection
Starting crane removal or rooftop demo before the permit is issued and posted
Not providing equipment submittals or gas piping details, which can stall commercial review
Submitting permit application without verifying current contractor registration status if the contractor also works under any separate city or state registration requirement
Skipping rooftop access, curb, or clearances on the plan set, which can trigger correction comments

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through the City of Boise Accela portal: Phone: (208) 384-3830. Boise’s building division is typically 1-5 business days for simple trade inspections, but commercial work should be scheduled as early as possible; verify current lead time with the permit desk before you need the crane or rooftop crew back on site.

inspections.description: Inspector verifies the RTU is set on the curb, equipment matches approved submittals, duct connections are sealed, condensate drain is trapped and sloped correctly, clearances are maintained, and the disconnect/control wiring is properly installed before startup.

inspections.description: Inspector checks gas piping pressure test results, shutoff valve location, appliance connector or hard pipe connection, sediment trap if required, proper support of gas piping, and leak-free operation at the RTU.

pro_tips: Have the RTU cut sheet, gas input rating, and curb dimensions ready before opening the Accela application; Boise commercial review moves faster when the submittal is complete the first time.
If the gas line is being touched at all, schedule the gas pressure test before the crane day so you are not paying the crew to wait.
inspector early; commercial final approval often depends on startup being witnessed or documented.
Check your Boise contractor registration and license status before starting the application if your company also works under any separate local registration requirement.
Bring photos of the existing unit nameplate and curb condition; they help resolve equipment substitution questions quickly.
